title: The faked-seam lesson moves into the craft layer every project receives
action: The lesson this feature paid for is sitting in the wrong layer. `docs/knowledge/` is THIS repo's own knowledge and travels nowhere; `.bee/expertise/` is craft that holds in any repo and onboarding copies it into every project it touches (`copy_expertise`, onboard/apply.rs). The pattern `docs/knowledge/patterns/20260821-a-faked-seam-hides-the-parse.md` names nothing bee-specific — it is about test doubles and external tools — so it belongs in `.bee/expertise/tests.md` as well. Read that pattern file first; it carries the claim, the evidence and the check already, and this cell restates them in the craft file's own voice rather than pasting them. Add ONE new bolded rule to the existing `## Fakes over stubs over mocks` section (line 190), placed after the existing 'A double is called with whatever the production code chooses to send' rule and before the 'If a test needs many doubles' one, so the section keeps building from what a double knows toward what it hides. The rule to state: a double at a seam that crosses a process boundary exercises the SEAM and never the PARSE behind the real implementation — the extraction that turns the external tool's actual reply into a value the code acts on. A fake returns whatever the test configured, so that extraction is the one thing no test through the fake can falsify, and a whole suite stays green while it is wrong. Carry the evidence in one compressed sentence, without bee or herdr vocabulary — a suite of over two thousand tests was green while a real extraction read the wrong path out of an external tool's JSON reply and returned nothing every time, so every live call through that path failed. Then the check, which is the part that must be actionable in any language: when a change adds a call to an external tool, capture one real reply and pin the extraction to that captured text in a test, writing the extraction as a pure function over a string so the test needs no process. Close by naming the consequence plainly: a green suite over a faked seam is not evidence that the path crossing the real boundary works. Second, a ONE-LINE cross-reference only: the `## Test the real code, never the twin` section (line 327) already ends with 'A passing test is not proof the real path ran' about fallbacks; append a sentence pointing at the new rule for the sibling case where the real path is never reached because a double stood in for it. Keep the file's voice: short paragraphs, bolded rule sentences, no bullet lists where prose serves. Change nothing else in the file — no reordering, no renumbering, no edits to any other section.
verify: rg -n 'faked seam|crosses a process boundary|captured|pure function over a string' .bee/expertise/tests.md; rg -c '^## ' .bee/expertise/tests.md
